checks.name: f4-abort-keeps-queue
checks.why: One job, no other extension before shell-jobs, no /reload, no user prompt: an abort that keeps the queue (the RPC abort, ctx.abort() with no abortHandler, or /compact, /new, /resume or /fork in the TUI) does not cause a second send (path F4 is closed). repro-f2.mts --one-job --keep-queue and --compact reach it live.

checks.name: old-f4-abort-keeps-queue

checks.name: f5-send-after-abort
checks.why: One job, no other extension before shell-jobs, no /reload, no user prompt, and only aborts that clear the queue (Esc in the TUI): a job that ends after Esc cleared the queue, while the aborted run winds down, lands once (path F5 is closed). repro-f2.mts --one-job --job-after-abort reaches it live.

checks.name: old-f5-send-after-abort
checks.why: The code before the fix, under the same conditions: path F5. Esc in the TUI clears the queue, the job ends before the run stops, its completion stays in the queue, and the reconcile of agent_settled sends it again.

checks.name: pi-run-start-fails
checks.note: The other path that the fix leaves open: /reload passes its isStreaming check, a completion starts a run, shell-jobs parks, so that run's before_agent_start reaches no shell-jobs handler, and the run then fails in _prepareRun. The "pending" hold has no copy in Pi.

checks.name: pi-deferred-throws
checks.note: The path that the fix leaves open: a deferred action before a deferred completion throws, Pi drops the completion, and its "pending" hold has no copy in Pi.

checks.name: pi-deferred-throws-no-duplicate
checks.note: Deferred actions that throw and runs that fail to start (DEFERRED_THROWS, RUN_START_FAILS), with noStuckHold and noHoldPastSettle off: they give no duplicate and break no other invariant.

checks.name: pi-deferred-throws-one-job-runs6
checks.note: One job and 6 user runs or aborts, with failed run starts: a resend whose run fails to start is lost, so a job can reach the attempt cap. The base of mutant-attempt-cap-off-by-one.

checks.name: survivor-send-ignores-binding
checks.why: lib/shell-jobs-delivery.ts:71 without `runtime.delivery !== binding`. Under the Pi fix no reconcile runs while the old send waits, so the old binding's send cannot make a second message. The check stops a send through the old API: once Pi invalidates the old runner, sendMessage throws (dist/core/extensions/loader.js:305-307) and the message waits for the next reconcile. The model has no liveness property for that delay. The conformance replay catches this change.

checks.name: mutant-reconcile-ignores-outbox
checks.mirrors: lib/shell-jobs-delivery.ts:132 without `|| runtime.outbox.has(job.id)`: reconcile counts an attempt for a send that is still in flight

checks.name: mutant-claim-unchecked
checks.mirrors: extensions/shell-jobs.ts:204 without `done.claimed` and lib/shell-jobs-delivery.ts:73 without `latest.claimed`: a job that the user killed gets a completion

checks.name: mutant-finalize-ignores-claim
checks.mirrors: extensions/shell-jobs.ts:204 without `done.claimed`: finalize counts an attempt for a job that the user killed. sendCompletion still drops the send (lib/shell-jobs-delivery.ts:73), so only the count breaks

checks.name: survivor-reconcile-ignores-idle
checks.why: lib/shell-jobs-delivery.ts reconcileDeliveries without the ctx.isIdle() check. Before the fix this broke oneCompletion. With the fix, a completion that Pi holds is held, so reconcile skips it also while Pi is busy. The check stays in the code: it keeps reconcile out of a compaction and a run, which the model does not cover.
